Subject: Demo + compute sizing call — preliminary recap

Hi Samir / team,

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Pain points you shared
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak inference bursts (current p99 spikes > 600ms) causing customer timeouts
- Sensitive data (PHI) in prompts; must run in a dedicated, isolated environment under customer-controlled networking
- Cost volatility from preemptible/spot GPUs and a lot of retry traffic; need predictable monthly unit economics
- Need to support ~60–100 QPS at peak with bursts up to ~150 QPS for short windows

Business goals
- Pilot in Q1 2027 (6–8 week PoC) to validate latency and isolation
- Achieve p99 < 200ms for key API paths and consistent throughput for 95% of traffic
- Keep inference unit cost within a target range that lets product team scale users without margin erosion

What we recommend (high level)
1) Dedicated reserved pool (isolation + SLA) — two sizing options to evaluate 
   - Option A: 6x A100-style nodes (higher perf, lower concurrency variance)
   - Option B: 12x A10-style nodes (more headroom for concurrency, lower per-node cost)
2) Autoscale/burst policy: 30% burst headroom for short spikes; can fall back to hosted variant for non-critical paths
3) KV/prefix caching + quantized runtimes (int8) to reduce pass-through cost and memory pressure
4) Ops/rollout: canary traffic split, warm KV caches, and a staged SLA ramp (dev -> canary -> prod)

Deliverables we can prepare next week
- Preliminary capacity workbook (attachment) with steady-state vs burst sizing
- 2-option commercial sketch (reserved vs reserved+burst) and estimated monthly unit costs
- SOW draft and timeline for a 6–8 week PoC

Ask from you
- Confirm primary security contact for SOC2/PHI checklist (we noted Rajiv Kulkarni on the call)
- Confirm procurement contact for pricing and SOW (we'll share a ballpark in the follow-up)

I'll loop Rohan (ops + sizing) and Marissa (commercial) on the next messages to propose concrete numbers.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: NeuroLoop — ops sizing and suggested configuration (v0)

Hi Samir / Elena — looping in ops-sizing details from our side. I'll be the primary ops contact for the PoC and run the tech deep-dive. See notes and assumptions below; I attached a workbook with the math.

Assumptions (from call)
- Peak QPS target: 100 QPS steady, bursts to 150 QPS for 5–10 minute windows
- P99 target: <200ms for the small prompt/response path (<= 512 tokens total)
- Workload mix: 70% short (<=128 tokens), 25% medium (128–512), 5% long (>512)
- Model baseline: 13B dense + some experiments with a quantized 30B variant

Sizing sketch (technical)
- Option A (higher perf): 6 x A100-class nodes with 80GB VRAM (good for 13B dense with headroom). Expected concurrency per node: ~140 concurrent small requests with batching.
- Option B (value scale): 12 x A10-class nodes. Concurrency per node lower but more parallel slots; better for heavy burst smoothing.
- KV cache: persistent LRU cache sized for 500k keys (shared across pool) — reduces expensive prefix recomputation
- Quantization: int8 path recommended for 30B tests; performance gains reduce tokens/sec cost ~25–35% in our benchmarks

SLAs and fallback
- Proposed target: p99 < 180ms on dedicated pool for the short prompt path, with 99.5% availability SLA during business hours for the PoC phase
- Fallback policy: if pool utilization > 85% or an availability event occurs, non-critical traffic shifts to a hosted fallback model (lower cost, higher latency) until headroom is restored

Estimated economics (very rough ballpark)
- Option A: ~$45k–$60k / month (reserved pool, fixed nodes + baseline support)
- Option B: ~$30k–$42k / month (reserved + more autoscale reliance)
- PoC commercial: 6–8 week reduced-rate engagement — we can outline options in the SOW

Next steps
1) Schedule a technical deep-dive (90m) next week — items: network/KMS requirements, perf benchmarks, canary plan
2) I'll share the ops workbook and a first-pass SOA/SOW draft by end of day tomorrow
3) Jordan will follow with a commercial sketch for Elena to review

If the sizing sketch looks reasonable, propose we book the deep-dive for Tue or Wed next week — do you have a preferred day/time?

Thanks — Rohan
